headline: One `css()` call in a component body is the whole gap between `bamboo` at 0.508 ms/1k and `panda` at 5.14 on a byte-identical source file: one compiles the call away, the other resolves it per render.

microbench.why: With a single level there is nothing to compose, so the case measures what each library does per element. `next-yak-9.7` folds its wrapper away and renders at 0.448 ms/1k, ahead of `vanilla`'s 0.502. `bamboo` and `panda` ship the same source file, one `css()` object literal inside the component, and land 10.1× apart: `bamboo` at 0.508 because its Vite plugin replaces the call with the resulting class string, `panda` at 5.14 because `css()` resolves the object to atomic classes on every render, 5.59 ms of component self-time. Depth is not the variable here, build-time evaluation is.

autocannon.why: `next-yak-9.7` serves 1751 req/s, `vanilla` 1562 and `bamboo` 1345, all bounded by writing markup. `panda` answers 161 req/s from the same source, re-resolving its `css()` call per element per request. `goober` (979) and `emotion` (435) pay a hash instead.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

attribution.why: The folded lane renders in 0.609 ms with a 0.255 ms library slice, and `stylex`, `next-yak-css-9.7` and `bamboo` follow within 0.035 ms of it, none with a styling package on the hot path. `panda` spends 5.59 of its 6.10 ms in component self-time on the same JSX. `emotion` splits the other way, 1.15 ms of library time against 0.710 ms of React, and `styled-components` 0.784 ms.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

hydrate.why: Hydration is pure JS for every static-sheet lane, 45.8-49.7 ms with 0 ms of style and layout in the span. `goober` and `styled-components` inject during hydration and record 0.19-0.20 ms of recalc plus a layout pass, landing at 100 and 105 ms. Spreads in the fast cluster run to 50%, so its order is a tie.

inp.why: Re-rendering one element costs 0.38-0.78 ms of JS in every lane except `panda`, which re-resolves its `css()` call for 1.12 ms and lands at 22.7 ms, the only shipped lane an interaction reaches. Everything else falls between 6.7 and 8.0 ms, inside the noise of a 33 ms frame.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Cold mount separates lanes by how much sheet the browser parses and how much JS runs before paint. The build-time lanes cluster at 70.6-74.3 ms, while `emotion` (111 ms), `styled-components` (102 ms) and `goober` (101 ms) build their sheet first. `panda` at 102 ms resolves its `css()` call for every element before that first paint.

renderTiming.why: One recalculation and one layout per lane, with the recalc costing 0.129-0.179 ms. A single-level tree gives the browser nothing to differentiate.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships 2.67 kB gzipped and `vanilla` 2.70. Atomic naming costs bytes twice, in the sheet and in the markup, so `bamboo` reaches 4.94 kB and `stylex-layers` 5.62, and `panda` adds its resolver for 7.05 kB. `cnfast` (14.8 kB) and `tailwind-merge` (13.8 kB) ship a scanned utility sheet regardless of what the page uses.

nsweep.why: At 4000 instances the folded lane holds 1.85 ms and the rest of the build-time field 2.06-2.16, all linear in n. `panda` reaches 22.2 ms, its per-element `css()` resolution multiplied by n, and `emotion` 8.70. `bamboo` stays at 2.16 ms running the source `panda` runs at 22.2.

crossCase: `compose-1` is the control of the composition ladder (the Examples `compose-3` and `compose-6` below). It fixes depth at one so the ladder's later gaps can be read as depth cost: the css-prop fold holds 0.522, 0.517 and 0.517 ms/1k across the three, the styled fold 0.448 to 0.686 to 0.698, while `bamboo` climbs 0.508 to 0.793 to 1.12 and `stylex-layers` 0.530 to 0.934 to 1.36 as each level adds a merge.
